RECAP

Braves Rout Mohawks En Route to Semi-Finals

 

July 27, 2015

The Braves kicked off the playoffs this weekend with an opening round Battle of the Tribes game against Mohawks Hockey. The Braves went 2-0 during the season against the Mohawks outscoring them 15-4. Will Cawkell got the start once again, in the early matchup and; Jeff Micheli provided suppot in place of healthy scratch Alex Pagnotta. 

 

The Braves got on the board first at 8:37 in the 1st period when Lucas Brutto netted his first of the campaign assisted by Anthony Paolucci and Stefano Ardizzi. The Mohawks would get a few chances but Will Cawkell remained solid. The Braves extended their lead to 2-0 when Jeff Micheli scored with 2:50 remaining off a booming slapshot assisted by Stefano Ardizzi. 

 

The Braves opened the door wider with 14:46 in the 2nd when Mark Pastore scored on a hustle breakout with assists from Cam Buchanan and Adam Brutto. The Mohawks countered just 1:25 later to stop the bleeding at 3-1. Anthony Paolucci responded at 11:12 scoring on a snapshot from the slot assisted by linemates Stefano Ardizzi and Lucas Brutto for a 4-1 lead. Mark Pastore would make it a 5-1 lead scoring his second of the game at 10:18 on a top of the circle drag and shoot assisted by Cam Buchanan  and Jeff Micheli. The Mohawks would stay within reach cutting the deficit to 5-2 at 7:02 but Mark Pastore would complete his hatrick scoring at 5:47 from Quenton Hunt and Adam Brutto to triple the Mohawks up 6-2. On the next shift, Keith Pearsoll found the back of the net on a hashmarks wristshot assists from Justin Carosi and Ryan Logue. Lucas Brutto would serve 4 minutes on behalf of goaltender Will Cawkell who drew a double minor for slashing.  Stefano Ardizzi widened the margin with a wristshot off the rush assisted by Ryan Logue and Mark Pastore would make it 9-2 with his fourth goal of the game assisted by Marco Congiusti. Jeff Micheli was called for roughing with 1:37 remaining but the Braves penalty kill would see the game into the intermission with the scoreboard at 9-2. 

 

Mark Pastore scored his fifth goal of the game at 11:03 in the 3rd assisted by Jeff Micheli and Adam Brutto to further extend the lead to 10-2. Cam Buchanan scored at 5:30 to make it 11-2 assists from Mark Pastore and Adam Brutto. The Mohawks would manage one more goal at 4:34 to make it 11-3 and Keith Pearsoll added the icing to the cake scoring his second of the game with an assist from Justin Carosi for a final score of 12-3.

 

Mark Pastore led the charge scoring 5 goals in the game giving him an all time team high of 21 during this Summer 2015 campaign. With 4 assists in the game Adam Brutto ties a single game record set by Ryan Logue on July 9, 2013. The Braves will faceoff on August 9th against the Maple Wolves in the Division Semi-Final game. During the regular season the Braves were outmatched by the Maple Wolves losing the season series 0-1-1 and were also outscored 10-6. The winner of that match will book a date to the Division Finals on August 16th against the winner of the Nifty Mittens/Vaughan Indies series.

RECAP

Braves Undefeated Streak Extended to 10 Games With 5-3 Win Over Muffalo Shavers

 

January 21, 2018

 

The Braves took on the Muffalo Shavers this week in their B Division debut. After a 9 game undefeated streak the Braves were promoted to the Gatorade Division marking the highest level of play the team has competed in during its 5 year history. At game time, Alex Pagnotta, Stephen Logue, Michael Congiusti, Stefano Ardizzi and Xav O'Krafka were listed as healthy scratches with Andrew Pozzebon making his 3rd straight start and Stephen Keane, Neil Baghel and Mark Arruda rounding out the support. 

 

The 1st period started with a rude awakening for the Braves as the Muffalo Shavers scored at 9:29 to make it 1-0. At 7:19 the Braves got a chance to regroup when the Muffalo Shavers were called 2 minutes for hooking. The Muffalo Shavers scored shorthanded to make it 2-0 at 6:34 shutting the Braves out after 1 period of play. 

 

At 5:27 Justin Carosi made it 2-1 scoring his 6th of the year assisted by Mark Arruda. The game was then tied 2-2 by Stephen Keane's 3rd of the season at 4:47 assisted by Ben Sherritt. The Muffalo Shavers regained a 3-2 lead scoring at 4:21 only to be tied back up again 3- 3 at 4:00 by Keith Pearsoll's 6th of the season , assisted by Cameron Buchanan and Lorcan Duffy. Dylan Brennan would round out the scoring for the period giving the Braves a 4-3 lead at 3:12 with his 8th of the year. 

 

At 4:26 in the 3rd period Cameron Buchanan, with his 6th of the year, scored the Braves insurance goal assisted by Lorcan Duffy and Dylan Brennan. Cam's goal also counts as the Braves 2000th point in franchise history. The Muffalo Shavers would get one more opportunity with 11 seconds left when Andrew Pozzebon was called 2 minutes for Roughing however nothing would come of it resulting in a 5-3 Braves win, their 10th consecutive game earning at least 1 point. 

 

Justin Carosi was awarded the Tomahawk of the game for scoring the Braves 1st goal of B Division play. The Braves will get a short rest this week as they take to the ice this Tuesday at 10pm against the Hawks. This season the Braves a 2-2-0 against the Hawks and have not lost since losing to the Hawks back on October 22, 2017. It will be important for the Braves to grab 2 interdivisional points this week to pad their record in the Gatorade Division.

Second Period Rally Costs Braves

 

March 24, 2014

 

The Braves took on Mohawks Hockey this week in last game of the regular season. After clinching first place last week, the Braves were looking to further extend their first place lead and go into the playoffs on a high note.
 
The Braves started strong in the first period with Mario Provenzano scoring his 2nd goal of the season from a near impossible angle at the side of the net allowing the Braves to take a 1-0 lead into the first intermission.
 
Captain Mark Pastore was able to put another one by the Mohawks goalie early in the second period and Ben Sherritt fired his 36th of the season past on a slapshot from just inside the Mohawks blue line giving the Braves a commanding 3-0 lead. Midway through the second, trouble started for the Braves when the Mohawks were able to score 2 goals in the span of 30 seconds to bring the game to within 1 goal.
 
The Mohawks were then able to convert on the powerplay on a penalty earned by Stephen Logue to tie the game at 3 goals apiece.  The Braves despite their best efforts to get something started were not able to muster any goals for the rest of the period and the game headed into the second intermission deadlocked in a tie. 
 
Luck and refereeing was not on the Braves side in this game as the Mohawks were able to score once again in the third period with 4 minutes remaining to take a 4-3 lead. The Braves once again pulled the goalie in an effort to secure a tie however with a scramble in front of the net and 5 seconds remaining on the clock, Mohawks players pushed the net off of the marshpegs to stop play dead despite the puck entering the net prior to this. The Braves were able to get one more faceoff in the opposing end however the fate of the game was sealed.
 
The Braves have clinched 1st place in the division and have earned themselves a first round matchup against the 4th placed Oilers, a team they have strugged with this season going 0-2-1 in three matchups. The Braves will need to matchup well defensively against the Oilers and will need their forwards to produce early and often to ensure playoff sucess.

Braves Shutout by Man Chest Hair United

December 8, 2014

 

The Braves were in action once again Sunday night taking on Man Chest Hair United. The Braves had taken on Man Chest Hair United only once before on Feburary 9th, 2014 during the 2013/14 Winter season resulting in the two teams skating away with a point each in a 2-2 tie.

 

The first period started off strong for both teams with the play bouncing from end to end and each team getting some strong scoring chances. Both goaltenders played well in this frame going on to deny every shot that came their way. Stephen Logue was exceptionally sharp early in the game giving his team a chance. The Braves were called for a 2 minute minor penalty for unsportsmanlike conduct when goalie Stephen Logue shoved one of the Man Chest Hair players for playing chippy in front. The Braves would go on to kill the powerplay but would be called for another one as Julian Kercz was called for roughing in defense of his goaltender. The Braves would once again kill that penalty and head into the second period still tied 0-0.

 

The second period was more of the same with both teams going end to end however both goaltenders stood on their heads. The Braves would have some powerplay opportunities in the second however no offense could be generated by either side sending the game into the third period still deadlocked at 0-0.

 

The Braves Julian Kercz drew a penalty in the third period for holding giving his team a chance on the powerplay to score the games elusive first goal. The powerplay unit was holding strong in the Man Chest Hair end when Ryan Logue's pass to the point did not make it to defenseman Adam Brutto resulting in a turnover which was subsequently skated to the other end for the games first goal. Man Chest Hair would go on to score their second goal of the game still shorthanded on the same penalty kill when Stephen Logue's pass in the defensive zone was intercepted by a Man Chest Hair player.

 

The Braves would get one more powerplay opportunity in the game however they could not generate any offense whatsoever in this affair taking their first regular season shutout since November 24, 2013 when the Bastone's blanked the Braves 1-0 with backup Will Cawkell in net. Despite the loss, Braves goaltender Stephen Logue gets another nod in this game as he went on to make some absolutely impossible saves to keep his team in the game. The Braves will get an early chance at redemption as they faceoff once again against Man Chest Hair United next week in another 8:45pm start.

Offense Awakens and Braves Book Ticket to the Finals

 

April 20, 2015 

 

The Braves took on Mohawks Hockey this weekend in the SVHL Dasani Division Semi-Finals. Last weeks game resulted in a 3-3 tie setting the stage for the winning team of this game to advance to the Finals. The Braves would seek help from backup goaltender Will Cawkell to get them over the hump. 

 

The 1st period featured many end to end chances with both goaltenders remaining steadfast. Both teams would get chances on the powerplay but would fail to convert sending the game into the first intermission still knotted in a 0-0 draw.

 

The Braves would strike first early in the 2nd period when Mark Pastore scored off assists from Alex Pagnotta and Michael Congiusti to put the Braves up by 1 with 9:48 remaining. Mark's goal would be followed up shortly when Ryan Logue netted his 2nd goal of the playoffs off feeds from Justin Carosi and Adam Brutto to extend the Braves margin to 2-0. The Mohawks would get another chance on the powerplay when Julian Kercz took to the box for a 2 minute minor however the Mohawks would not manage to counter until they caught a break with only 0:02 remaining in the frame to cut the deficit back to 1.

 

Mark Pastore would kick of the 3rd period with his 2nd goal of the game off feeds from Ryan Logue and Alex Pagnotta with 8:47 remaining to restore the Braves 2 goal lead. Mark would go on to net his 3rd goal of the game mid-way through the 3rd period to solidify his hatrick and further extend the Braves lead to 3 goals. Adam Brutto would serve 2 minutes in the box alongside his Mohakws counterpart on a coincidental minor on behalf of goaltender Will Caukel following a scrum in front of the net. Ryan Logue would go on to put  the final nail in the coffin with 4:36 remaining to extend the Braves lead to 4 goals. The two teams would skate away the balance of the game resulting in the Braves moving forward to next week's finals. 

 

The results of the Cherry Blasters/Shemlts game are still pending and the Braves await the news of who they will be facing in the finals. With his win on the night, Will Cawkell evens his all time Braves record to 2-2 with an impressive lifetime 1.25 GAA. Mark Pastore's hat trick in the game gives him an impressive 5 goals in the playoffs and Ryan Logue's pair of goals pushes him to the top of the Braves playoff leaderboard with a total of 3 goals and 3 assists.
